methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort study with consecutive patient enrollment (n=298, 2000-2022). Clear patient characteristics and outcomes reported with standardized case ascertainment (radiology/pathology confirmation of HCC recurrence). Appropriate multivariate analysis with competing risks accounting for death without recurrence as competing event. Hazard ratios with 95% CIs throughout. Limitations acknowledged: single-center design, temporal heterogeneity, MVI measured dichotomously rather than refined grading. Proper statistical approach mitigates some design limitations.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: External validation of RETREAT score for predicting post-transplant HCC recurrence in European setting different from original derivation cohort. Directly applicable to clinical decision-making: surveillance intensity, immunosuppression selection, identification of candidates for future adjuvant therapy. RETREAT already used in clinical practice; this validation strengthens confidence in its generalizability across expanded selection criteria and down-staging strategies.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive STROBE adherence: clear objectives and methods, participant flow documented, baseline characteristics in Table 1, statistical methods detailed (Kaplan-Meier, log-rank, Cox regression). Results systematically presented with 95% CIs and follow-up times. Strengths and limitations thoroughly discussed. Some gaps: no explicit data availability or code sharing statement, no pre-registration mentioned. Supplementary tables referenced but content not independently verified.

novelty_literature.justification: RETREAT score published by Mehta et al. (2017) and subsequently validated in multiple studies cited (references 18-21). This manuscript represents another external validation rather than novel discovery. Contributions are study-specific (extended 2-decade follow-up, competing risks analysis, single-center standardization) but methodologically and conceptually incremental to existing RETREAT literature.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear narrative arc positioning RETREAT in evolving transplant landscape. Introduction effectively contextualizes expanded criteria and down-staging strategies. Methods comprehensive with appropriate technical detail. Results logically presented via tables and Kaplan-Meier curves. Discussion thoroughly explores both strengths (long follow-up, competing risks) and limitations (single-center, temporal heterogeneity). Professional writing quality suitable for high-impact publication.

key_strengths: Extended long-term follow-up (median 64 months, up to 15 years) capturing real-world evolution of transplant practice with transition from Milan to Up-to-Seven criteria and increased down-staging use
Competing risks analysis appropriately accounting for death without recurrence, demonstrating RETREAT remains robust prognostic factor (HR 6.4 for high-risk vs low-risk)
Standardized single-center practice across two decades reduces procedural and management variability while demonstrating generalizability across heterogeneous eligibility policies
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design limits generalizability despite being Italian validation; multicenter studies remain gold standard
MVI assessed dichotomously (present/absent) rather than using refined grading systems that capture extent and distribution, potentially underestimating prognostic information
RETREAT+ model testing shows no improvement over original RETREAT, suggesting study did not advance mechanistic understanding of recurrence determinants
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid external validation of established RETREAT score with methodological strengths (competing risks analysis, long-term follow-up). Appropriate tier 3 venue for confirmatory evidence that strengthens clinical confidence but does not introduce novel concepts.
